Continuous Pipeline Quality: SLOs, SLIs & Data Drift

11 min read Updated: November 2026 By Rajvardhan Singh Rathore
Treat your data pipeline like a production distributed application. Learn how to define concrete Service Level Objectives (SLOs) for freight data freshness and detect silent statistical data drift.
Defining Logistics Data SLIs and SLOs

Modern data contracts require explicit mathematical SLIs:

  • Freshness SLI: Percentage of shipment events available in the warehouse within 5 minutes of physical scan ($99.5\%$ target).
  • Completeness SLI: Percentage of rows containing non-null carrier codes and tracking numbers ($99.9\%$ target).
  • Accuracy SLI: Percentage of GPS coordinates passing geofence containment ($99.0\%$ target).

Error Budget Consumption & Alert Tiers

A $99.9\%$ monthly completeness SLO permits an error budget of 0.1% bad records. If a sudden surge consumes > 20% of the 30-day error budget in a single hour, automated multi-window alerts fire to the on-call data reliability engineer.

Detecting Statistical Data Drift in SQL

Track distribution shifts in daily payload metrics (such as average parcel weight or status code frequency) using Z-score outlier detection:

PostgreSQL Drift Detection SQL 
WITH daily_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    DATE(event_timestamp) AS event_date,
    COUNT(*) AS daily_volume,
    AVG(gross_weight_kg) AS avg_weight,
    STDDEV(gross_weight_kg) AS std_weight
  FROM fct_shipment_milestones
  GROUP BY DATE(event_timestamp)
),
historical_baseline AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(daily_volume) AS mean_vol,
    STDDEV(daily_volume) AS std_vol
  FROM daily_stats
  WHERE event_date < CURRENT_DATE
)
SELECT 
  d.event_date,
  d.daily_volume,
  ROUND(((d.daily_volume - b.mean_vol) / NULLIF(b.std_vol, 0))::numeric, 2) AS volume_z_score,
  CASE 
    WHEN ABS((d.daily_volume - b.mean_vol) / NULLIF(b.std_vol, 0)) > 3.0 
    THEN 'ANOMALY: Severe Volume Drift'
    ELSE 'NORMAL'
  END AS drift_status
FROM daily_stats d
CROSS JOIN historical_baseline b
WHERE d.event_date = CURRENT_DATE;
